verses.text: How terrible for you, destroyer, who has never been destroyed! How terrible for you, traitor, who has never been betrayed! When you finish destroying, you will be destroyed. When you finish betraying, you will be betrayed.
LORD, be kind to us. We wait for you. Be our strength every morning and our salvation in times of trouble.
At the sound of your thunder, the peoples run away. When you rise up, the nations scatter.
Your enemies' goods will be gathered up as caterpillars strip a field. People will rush on them like a swarm of locusts.
The LORD is lifted high, for he lives in heaven. He will fill Zion with justice and righteousness.
He will be the firm foundation of your times, a rich store of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. Deep respect for the LORD is your treasure.
Look, their brave men cry out in the streets. The messengers who hoped for peace weep bitterly.
The highways are empty. No one travels on the roads. The covenant has been broken. Its witnesses are rejected. No one is respected.
The land mourns and dries up. Lebanon is ashamed and withers. Sharon is like a desert, and Bashan and Carmel have lost their leaves.
"Now I will rise up," says the LORD. "Now I will show my power. Now I will be lifted high.
Your plans are like dry grass, and what you produce is like straw. Your own breath is a fire that will burn you up.
The peoples will be burned to powder like lime, like thorn bushes cut down and thrown into the fire.
You who are far away, listen to what I have done! You who are near, see how powerful I am!"
The sinners in Zion are terrified. The godless are shaking with fear. They ask, "Who of us can live with this consuming fire? Who of us can live with this fire that burns forever?"

The one who lives right and speaks the truth, who refuses to get rich by cheating others, who keeps their hands from taking bribes, who closes their ears to plans of murder, and shuts their eyes so as not to look at evil,
that person will live on the heights. Their safe place will be a fortress of rock. They will be given food, and their water will never run out.
Your eyes will see the King in his beauty. You will see a land that stretches far away.
You will think back on the time of terror and say, "Where is the official who counted? Where is the one who weighed the tribute money? Where is the officer who counted the towers?"
You will no longer see those proud and fierce people, those people with a strange language you could not understand, with their stammering speech that made no sense.

Look at Zion, the city where we celebrate our festivals. Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful place to live, a tent that will never be moved. Its tent pegs will never be pulled up, and none of its ropes will be broken.
There the LORD will be our Mighty One. It will be like a place of wide rivers and streams, but no enemy ship with oars will row there, and no mighty warship will sail there.
For the LORD is our judge. The LORD is our lawgiver. The LORD is our king. He is the one who will save us.
Your ship's ropes hang loose. They cannot hold the mast steady or spread out the sail. Then a huge amount of treasure will be divided up. Even the lame will carry off their share.
No one living in Zion will say, "I am sick." The people who live there will have their sins forgiven.
